split.strategy: StratifiedGroupKFold, 20 folds, groups = product_id, strata = recommendation x rating_band (missing as its own class); 14 folds train, 3 validation, 3 test, which folds go where is drawn with the seed

masking.rule: inside each recommendation class of the train part, sort by stable_hash(id) = int(sha256(f'{MASK_SEED}|{id}').hexdigest()[:16], 16) and mask the first floor(rate * class_count) rows; ties broken by id
masking.applies_to: train rows with a recommendation label; validation and test are never masked
masking.masked_rows_rating_band: masked rows leave supervised training completely, rating band included, so the hidden label cannot leak through the rating; their true labels are kept only in audit/masked_labels_reference.csv

rating_band.definition: low: 0 < rate < 2.5, medium: 2.5 <= rate < 4.0, high: 4.0 <= rate <= 5
rating_band.rate_zero_meaning: a rate of exactly 0 means no rating was recorded, so there is no band

text.body: raw text in every file; normalize with digikala_reviews.normalize before modeling
text.text_seen_in_train: true when the normalized text is identical to the text of any train row
text.how_to_read: digikala_reviews.standard_files.read_split_file(name). Plain pd.read_csv turns texts such as 'NA' or 'null' into missing values; only an empty label cell is missing

files.train_supervised.csv: train rows with at least one label; masked rows removed. A missing label means that head skips the row
files.train_pseudo_unlabeled.csv: masked train rows, id and body only
files.natural_unlabeled.csv: train rows without a recommendation label, id and body only. Rows among them that have a rating band are also in train_supervised for the band head
files.audit/masked_labels_reference.csv: true labels of the masked rows, only for checking pseudo-labels; never used for training
